blocks.text: Datasets derived from each recording (one file → several queryable layers): content (transcript, sealed by sha); timing (start/end, pcm offsets); speaker-local label + corpus cluster id; condition (codec/rate/channels); discoverable spectrum columns; codec tokens (content stream cb0, character stream cb1-7).

Discoverable-spectrum columns (14): duration_s, chars_per_s, energy_db_mean, energy_db_std, pause_ratio, f0_mean_hz, f0_std_semitones, f0_range_hz, voiced_ratio, spectral_centroid_hz, spectral_bandwidth_hz, spectral_rolloff_hz, spectral_flatness, zcr.
Split rule: speaker-cluster-disjoint; straddling sessions → train; admission 10% / dev 10% by cluster hash.

Classification-driven exclusions: raw audio never leaves the host (raw_media_exported=false); transcripts stay on the host (text_exported=false); presenter identity is a corpus-local cluster id — no voiceprint is stored; the sealed admission split is never read by training.

Results are on the dev split, which guides iteration; they are not admission evidence. Admission is decided only on the sealed, speaker-cluster-disjoint split by a separate evaluation run.

The dev split was requalified after the cluster-disjoint rule left it too small to measure: whole train sessions were promoted to dev (dev_basis=session_holdout), so presenter voices may overlap between train and dev. This is a disclosed selection effect on dev; the admission split is unchanged.
Language fidelity is a character-trigram judgement against each language's own profile; it is not a reading of meaning or story quality, which only native readers can judge.
